provenance.instrument: City of Pittston Zoning Code (Chapter 480 Zoning, Ord. No. 9-2019 of 11-20-2019, as amended by Ord. No. 14-2020 and Ord. No. 2-2024), with Chapter 270 Floodplain Management (Ord. No. 2-2024), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 PI3172, City of Pittston. 480-12 defines the City as 'The City of Pittston, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania', so this is Pittston city, Luzerne County, not Pittston Township. District use lists and bulk tables are text in Articles VIII to XIV. The one attachment is the zoning map. Chapter 480 sends floodplain matters to Chapter 270, and the stricter of the two applies. New Laws: Ord. No. 1-2026, 3-2026 and 8-2026 (Chapter 455), 2-2026 (Chapter 130), Res. No. 13214 (Chapter 30), Ord. No. 7-2026 (an agreement) and Ord. No. 6-2026 of 10-21-2026, a short-term rental license ordinance not yet codified, which names Chapter 480 zoning districts where a short-term rental license may issue
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows the version date 2026-01-21 beside the Code link, with New Laws (8). Chapter 480 history: Ord. No. 9-2019 of 11-20-2019, amended 10-21-2020 by Ord. No. 14-2020 and 2-15-2024 by Ord. No. 2-2024. The New Laws list Ord. No. 6-2026 (short-term rentals, 10-21-2026) as not yet codified
provenance.code_caution: Ord. No. 6-2026 of 10-21-2026 (short-term rental licenses) is adopted but not yet in the online code. Its search excerpt names zoning districts where a short-term rental license may issue. It was not read (PDF), so whether it changes Chapter 480 is not confirmed
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, elder cottage, tenant house, temporary dwelling, guest house, household employee, supplemental dwelling, care of) find only 'accessory living quarters' in the definitions. R-1, R-2 and R-3 list as accessory uses 'Accessory uses on the same lot and incidental to the principal uses (garages, accessory living quarters)' (480-36B(1), 480-39B(1), 480-42B(1))

Accessory living quarters are 'An accessory building used solely as the temporary dwelling of guests of the occupants of the premises; such dwelling having no kitchen facilities and not rented or otherwise used as a separate sleeping unit' (480-12). That is a guest building without a kitchen, not a dwelling unit, so it is not an ADU. Adding a kitchen or renting it takes it outside the definition. 'Temporary' means 'Lasting or designed to last not more than 90 days', so guests stay at most that long. A sleeping unit may have sanitation or a kitchen 'but not both' (480-12), while accessory living quarters may not be used 'as a separate sleeping unit'. The stronger reading: guests of the household only, with no kitchen

R-1, R-2, R-3, NC and CB allow 'not more than one principal dwelling structure and not more than two accessory buildings' on a lot (480-37B, 480-40B, 480-43B, 480-46B, 480-49B). A family is persons related by birth, marriage or adoption residing together (480-12)

Conversion of an existing one-family dwelling to two dwelling units for two families is a special exception in R-3 only: the units meet the City Building Code, one off-street space per unit, and all units are reached through a common entrance in the wall facing the street (480-42D(6), 480-144A). More than two units needs 1,000 sq ft per unit (480-144B)

Two-family attached or semidetached dwellings (one family wholly or partly over the other, in a building with one or two party walls in common with adjacent buildings) are permitted by right in R-2 (4,000 sq ft lot, 50 ft wide) and R-3 (7,000 sq ft lot, 50 ft wide). No two-family detached dwelling is listed (480-12, 480-39A(3), 480-40, 480-42A(3), 480-43). Multifamily dwellings are by right in R-3 (1,000 sq ft per unit, 60 ft wide) and by special exception in NC and CB (480-42A(1), 480-43, 480-45C(9), 480-48C(1))

Accessory buildings in R-1, R-2 and R-3 stand in the rear and side yards only, 5 ft from the side and rear lines (10 ft where the line abuts an alley), 10 ft from the main building, and at most 18 ft tall (480-75, 480-76, 480-78)

Parking: 2 spaces per dwelling unit for a single-family dwelling, 1.5 per unit for a two-family dwelling, 1 per unit for multifamily, and 1 per unit for a conversion (480-64, 480-144A(2)). A fraction counts as a space: 'any fractional parking space is computed as a whole space' (480-64A). The parking table does not apply in the Central Business District (480-64B)

Uses not provided for: in a nonresidential district (OS, NC, CB, I) a use not listed is prohibited unless the Zoning Hearing Board grants it as a special exception on proof that it is no more intensive than, and 'closely similar in impacts and character to', the uses permitted there (480-27). In R-1, R-2 and R-3 there is no such path. NC: the use chart (Table 480-27) lists single-family detached and single-family attached or semidetached dwellings by special exception, while the NC use list (480-45) does not name them. The code conflicts. CB lists no single-family dwelling

Floodplain (Chapter 270, Ord. No. 2-2024): the floodplain is the FIRM of June 20, 2024 or its latest revision and any community-identified flood hazard areas (270-17). An accessory structure in the floodplain may not be designed or used for human habitation, no variance is granted for one over 600 sq ft, and in an AE zone without a floodway no new construction may be within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit and no variance may raise the base flood elevation more than one foot in all. The regulatory flood elevation is the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft. New construction is a structure begun on or after the chapter's effective date, with its later improvements (270-18B(2)(b), 270-23E, 270-33B, C, 270-35). The stricter of Chapter 480 and Chapter 270 applies (Chapter 480 history note)

Every residential building needs a passageway at least 6 ft wide from the public way to the outside entrance of each dwelling unit, 2 ft wider for each story over two (480-93). There must be 10 ft of clear space between a main building and an accessory building, and 20 ft between a residential building and another main building on the lot (480-94). A project that needs more sewer, water or other services gets the providing agency's approval first, and permits may be denied where the services are not available (480-96)
Land development includes 'a group of two or more residential or nonresidential buildings, whether proposed initially or cumulatively' (480-12)

Nonconforming: additions to nonconforming structures must conform, and a structure housing a nonconforming use may not be enlarged to increase that use (480-127D). No section on building on a nonconforming lot of record was found in Article XXX
CB sets a minimum building height of 45 ft for new or infill construction (Table 480-49). The Main Street Overlay District sets design standards (Article XV, not read)
Variances: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of MPC 910.2 (480-22B). No bar on a use variance was found

term.note: Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, elder cottage, tenant house, temporary dwelling, guest house, household employee, supplemental dwelling and care of, and read the use lists of every district. The only near term is 'accessory living quarters', a guest building with no kitchen that may not be rented (480-12)

status.note: No district lists a dwelling unit accessory to a house. Accessory living quarters are guest rooms in an accessory building with no kitchen, not a unit. R-3 allows the conversion of a one-family dwelling to two units by special exception (480-144A), and R-2 and R-3 permit two-family attached or semidetached dwellings

path.note: A second dwelling unit on a house lot is not a listed use in R-1, R-2 or R-3, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). R-3 allows a conversion of a one-family dwelling to two units by special exception, and R-2 and R-3 permit two-family attached or semidetached dwellings (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of MPC 910.2. No bar on a use variance

unlisted_use_path.note: Only in a nonresidential district (OS, NC, CB, I): a use not listed may be a special exception if it is no more intensive than and closely similar to the uses permitted there. In R-2 and R-3 a second unit may be read as the listed two-family dwelling or conversion instead, and R-1, R-2 and R-3 have no unlisted-use path

unlisted_use_districts.note: 'within any nonresidential zoning district'. OS, NC, CB and I are read as the nonresidential districts

unlisted_use_scope.quote: The proposed use would be closely similar in impacts and character to uses permitted in that district

value.name: Conversion of a one-family dwelling to two dwelling units (R-3)
value.conditions: An existing one-family dwelling converted to two dwelling units for two families. The units meet the City Building Code. One off-street parking space for each unit. All units are reached through a common entrance in the wall of the building facing the street the lot fronts on. A passageway at least 6 ft wide from the public way to the entrance (480-93). The sewer and water providers approve the added unit (480-96)

requires.condition: An existing one-family dwelling to convert
A common entrance for both units in the wall facing the street

disputed_min_lot.note: The conversion section sets no lot size. Whether the 7,000 sq ft two-family lot of Table 480-43 applies to a converted house is not settled

value.note: A special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board (480-22C)

value.name: Two-family attached or semidetached dwelling (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: A building for two families, one living wholly or partly over the other, with one or two party walls in common with adjacent buildings. R-2: lot 4,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide, front 10 ft, side 10 ft in all with one at least 5 ft, rear 20 ft. R-3: lot 7,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide, front 5 ft, side 10 ft in all with one at least 5 ft, rear 10 ft. Height 35 ft. 1.5 parking spaces per unit, 3 in all. A passageway at least 6 ft wide from the public way to the outside entrance of each unit (480-93)

requires.condition: The building shares one or two party walls with adjacent buildings. A detached house is not a two-family attached or semidetached dwelling, and no two-family detached dwelling is listed

value.note: Read as a twin or row building whose house is divided into two stacked units

historic_bypass.note: No historic preservation path was found in the articles read

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. R-1, R-2 and R-3 list accessory living quarters (guest rooms, no kitchen). R-2 and R-3 list two-family attached or semidetached dwellings, and R-3 the conversion of a one-family dwelling

value.condition: 'There shall not be more than one principal dwelling structure and not more than two accessory buildings' on a lot.

In the floodplain an accessory structure that is not elevated 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have at most 200 sq ft of floor area. No variance is granted for an accessory structure over 600 sq ft, and a variance needs a signed nonconversion agreement.

disputed_by.note: 270-23E is the rule for an accessory structure that is not elevated or floodproofed. A garage raised so its lowest floor is at or above the regulatory flood elevation, and built as a residential structure, may not be reached. Work of 50% or more of its market value must fully comply (270-31C)

value.condition: In the floodplain (the FIRM of June 20, 2024 or its latest revision, and any community-identified flood hazard areas) new construction and substantial improvements have the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft. Nothing in the floodway may raise flood levels, and in an AE area without a floodway no variance may raise the base flood elevation more than one foot in all. Work of 50% or more of a building's market value, with improvements added up over the period the code sets, is a substantial improvement that must fully comply, and smaller work is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible. The stricter of Chapter 480 and Chapter 270 applies.
In an AE zone without a floodway no new construction or development may be located within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of a watercourse without a DEP permit.

types_allowed.note: No ADU use. A second unit is only possible through the listed paths

front_yard_barred.note: 'Accessory structures in R-1, R-2, and R-3 districts shall be permitted in the rear and side yards only'. A garage may stand in the front yard of a steep lot (480-77)

front_yard_barred_districts.note: 'Accessory structures in R-1, R-2, and R-3 districts shall be permitted in the rear and side yards only'. The bar is not stated for OS, NC, CB or I

separation_ft.note: 'All accessory buildings shall be separated from the main building by 10 feet'
